why: The SemiAnalysis report of the Kyber NVL144 slip to 2028 is exactly what the reasons already rely on for rung 2.
Google Cloud growth and backlog suggest strong demand, but give no quantified basis for four-company 2027 data-center capex at or above $1.2 trillion.
Google Cloud growth and backlog point to strong demand but do not quantify 2027 capex at or above $1.1 trillion; too weak to leave rung 3.
Firmus's backstopped Batam project is already part of the reasons' roughly $15B estimate; nothing new on the amount.
Chinese domestic chip suppliers being sold out speaks to demand, not to a Chinese permission decision or NVIDIA-confirmed H200 shipments.
Analyst NVIDIA revenue growth forecasts are indirect and unquantified for the four hyperscalers' 2027 capex; does not cross the $1.1 trillion boundary.
Full production and fall shipping to eight cloud partners is the reference the reasons already use for rung 1.
The $650 billion 2026 plan and NVIDIA's $1 trillion 2027 projection are already the reference in the reasons.
Google Cloud revenue and backlog growth lean upward but do not quantify the big four's 2026 data-center capex beyond $700 billion.
Selling more Oberon-Rubin racks supports Rubin shipping on schedule, the same direction as rung 1.
Analyst NVIDIA revenue growth forecasts do not quantify four-hyperscaler 2027 data-center capex; too weak to cross $1.2 trillion.
The $650 billion plan and NVIDIA's more-than-$1-trillion claim are the reference the reasons already use for rung 3.
Whether the backstop is expected to be drawn does not change the amount committed, which is what the question measures.
NVIDIA adding $3.5B of lease guarantees supports a willingness to guarantee leases, the same direction as the chosen Yes rung.
Memory market tightness lasting to 2028 does not bear on the big four's 2026 data-center capex total.
Cancelling the four-die Rubin Ultra signals further roadmap disruption, pointing the same way as the chosen No rung for Kyber by 2027.
Choosing Intel Xeon 6 as host CPU for DGX Rubin NVL8 is a design detail, not evidence about shipment timing.
NVIDIA's 'Our roadmap is intact' is already weighed in the reasons as a counterweight lacking specific timing.
NVIDIA denying a roadmap delay concerns its own products, not the four hyperscalers' 2027 capex total.
Selling more Oberon-Rubin racks to cover the shortfall confirms the Kyber delay, the same direction as the chosen No rung.
Whether NVIDIA or neoclouds intend to use the backstop says nothing about hyperscaler data-center capex.
Lease backstops could add commitments to the ~$9B estimate near the $10B boundary, but no amount is given and it is unclear they fall under the programme.
An Ohio lease guarantee could push the ~$9B estimate past $10B, but it was only in negotiation, unquantified, and may lie outside the AI-cloud programme.
Zuckerberg's remark on slow AI-agent progress is a vague caution, unquantified for 2027 capex; too weak to move rung 3.
Google Cloud growth and backlog lean upward but do not quantify the four companies' 2026 data-center capex past $700 billion.
The announcement of the revenue-sharing and credit-support model is already cited in the reasons as directional support.
A view that the market underestimates NVIDIA's second-half shipments is indirect and unquantified for the four hyperscalers' 2026 capex.
Repurchase of unsold GPU capacity describes the already-cited credit-support model, not the Ohio lease guarantee.
Sharon AI's $4.88B backstop is a precedent the reasons already cite; it is not itself an Ohio-lease guarantee.
NVIDIA starting to backstop data-center leases supports a signed Ohio guarantee, the same direction as the chosen Yes rung.
NVIDIA's quarterly revenue and margin guidance says nothing about Chinese authorization of the three named firms.
Zuckerberg's remark on slow AI-agent progress does not quantify any change to the four companies' 2026 data-center capex.
A claim that NVIDIA's China position stays at zero points to No, but its speaker and basis are unclear against the permission reports the reasons weigh.
Firmus's expected customer revenue sizes the project but not NVIDIA's committed credit support; the reasons' GPU-based estimate is unaffected.
Scrapping the two-rack backup plan does not bring Kyber forward; it points the same way as, or is neutral to, the chosen No rung.
A view that market shipment estimates are too low is indirect and unquantified for the big four's 2026 data-center capex.
Hyperscaler capex plans do not bear on whether NVIDIA signs the OpenAI Ohio lease guarantee.
